interview.name: Nell
interview.answer: They haven’t settled a time or place yet; the location is still unresolved.

reflections: Nell relies on secondhand updates and follows up by asking around when information is incomplete.
Ira is proactive and practical, offering to check on progress and relay what still needs doing.
Oren is honest about uncertainty and deferred attention, pointing Nell toward someone closer to the work.
Nell is trying to keep track of the repair drive through second-hand updates and is willing to relay information to others.
Several people are uncertain about the fence repair status, suggesting communication is fragmented and confirmation is still pending.
Hana and Oren both position themselves as checkers or confirmers, while Ira offers practical help on unfinished work.
Nell is acting as an information relay, repeatedly passing along second-hand updates and asking for quick confirmations.
The group is coordinating a practical repair effort, with multiple people offering to check details, bring tools, and point others to the next task.
Communication is collaborative but uncertain, with participants relying on brief follow-ups rather than firm firsthand knowledge.
Nell is mostly a relay point: she has partial information and keeps asking around before passing updates on.
Bo and Gus are both willing to help with the repair effort, but they need a clear meeting point or next step before acting.
The group is coordinating a fence repair drive through informal handoffs, with Rosa and the meetup location still unresolved.
Nell is the main coordinator, but she is still working with incomplete information and keeps promising follow-up updates.
Gus is willing to help practically by bringing tools and waiting for instructions, but he does not yet know the exact repair location.
Eli seems to have the clearest plan, anchoring the group with a specific meeting place and time at the community shed at 9.
